_comment: AI Incident Response Plan - seed asset for the ES Mission Control
mc_response_templates KV Store collection.
VALUES HERE ARE PLAIN TEXT. Mission Control stores response plan strings
URL-ENCODED (e.g. 'Identification%20(Detection%20and%20Analysis)'). The
Show post-deploy script encodes every string on write, including the SPL in
suggestions.searches - do not pre-encode this file, it is kept readable so
it stays reviewable in git.
SCHEMA: the authoritative source is the Python model at
missioncontrol/bin/blueridge/data_models/models/response_template.py, NOT
collections.conf - the latter only declares scalar/indexed types and omits
nested objects entirely, so its silence proves nothing.
ResponseTemplate: id, template_id, name, description, template_status,
creator, updated_by, is_default, active, used, version, ai_generated,
source_attachment_id, create_time, update_time, origin, phases[]
origin is a DICT {id, name, version} - a bare string raises TypeError in
ResponseTemplateOrigin(**origin) and breaks every read through the
/response_templates REST handler the ES UI uses.
ResponsePhase: name, order, tasks[]   (phase names must be unique)
ResponseTask: name, order, description, owner, tag, status,
is_note_required, notes[], files[], suggestions
suggestions: {searches[], actions[], playbooks[]}
searches[]  = {name, description, spl}  - native Splunk SPL, no SOAR
actions[]   = SOAR actions {last_job_id, name, description, action, type,
app_id, asset, parameters[]} - app_id/asset are the SOAR
tenant's numeric ids, so they are never hard-coded here
playbooks[] = SOAR playbooks {playbook_id, repo, ...}
Limits: name <= 250 chars, description <= 7000 chars.
SOAR BINDING: a task may carry suggestions.soar_binding[] = {app_name,
asset_name, action, type, name, description, parameters[]}. It is NOT a
Mission Control field: bin/genai_es_seed.py (run in-product by the shipped
search 'GenAI - ES - Seed Response Plan and SOAR Binding' via | genaiseedes,
and from outside by tools/show_postdeploy.py) resolves app_name/asset_name
against the paired SOAR, writes the result into suggestions.actions[] and
strips soar_binding before the record is written. When the app is not on
the paired SOAR the binding is dropped and whatever actions[]/playbooks[]
the live record already carries for that task is preserved (e.g. an
action attached in the ES UI).
Tasks DO carry embedded searches - that is what suggestions.searches is for,
and it is how the ES Triage agent is grounded in specific tooling rather
than prose. actions[]/playbooks[] are SOAR objects: the Containment tasks bind
the simulated 'MedAdvice Identity Provider' SOAR app (shipped in
default/data/soar_apps/) through soar_binding; the three simulated
ai_defense_* adaptive response actions stay named in the task descriptions
as the no-SOAR fallback.
BINDING: a response plan does NOT attach to a detection. The chain is
savedsearches.conf action.notable.param.investigation_type -> KV
mc_incident_types (_key = that name, response_template_ids = [template_id])
-> this record. Investigation type names must be LOWERCASE
(missioncontrol/bin/blueridge/incident_types.py rejects uppercase).
Placeholder tokens <actor>, <app> and <session> are replaced by the analyst
(or by the Triage agent) with values from the finding.
name: AI Incident Response Plan
description: Response plan for GenAI/LLM security incidents surfaced by Cisco AI Defense - prompt injection, jailbreak, guardrail bypass and AI-mediated data exposure. Phases follow NIST 800-61 adapted for AI systems. Also used to ground the ES Triage agent: the agent reasons against the plan assigned to the investigation.
creator: nobody

tasks.name: Validate the AI Defense verdict
tasks.description:
Confirm the block was a genuine policy violation rather than a false positive. Review the guardrail that fired, the policy name, and the classification returned by Cisco AI Defense.

Record in the task notes whether the verdict is confirmed, and the injection technique observed.

searches.name: Blocked prompts for this actor
searches.description: Every AI Defense block for the actor, with the guardrail, policy and classification that fired.
searches.spl:
index=gen_ai_log `exclude_scoring_sourcetypes` gen_ai.user.id="<actor>" gen_ai.policy.blocked="true"
| table _time, gen_ai.session.id, gen_ai.app.name, gen_ai.request.model, prompt_category, gen_ai.policy.name, gen_ai.guardrail.ids, risk_score
| sort - _time

tasks.name: Scope the campaign
tasks.description:
Establish breadth before containment. Determine how many attempts the actor made, across how many sessions, applications and models, and over what period.

If multiple applications or models were targeted, treat this as a deliberate campaign rather than an isolated attempt and escalate severity accordingly.

searches.name: Campaign scope for this actor
searches.description: Attempt count, distinct sessions, apps, models and first/last seen for the actor.
searches.spl:
index=gen_ai_log `exclude_scoring_sourcetypes` (gen_ai.user.id="<actor>" OR enduser.id="<actor>")
| stats count AS attempts, dc(gen_ai.session.id) AS sessions, dc(gen_ai.app.name) AS apps, dc(gen_ai.request.model) AS models, values(prompt_category) AS techniques, min(_time) AS first_seen, max(_time) AS last_seen BY gen_ai.user.id

tasks.name: Review prompts that were NOT blocked
tasks.description:
HIGHEST PRIORITY EVIDENCE. Any injection attempt from this actor that AI Defense allowed through is a guardrail gap - it reached the model and produced a real response. These determine whether this incident is contained or ongoing.

If the attached search returns any results, do not close as benign. Continue to Containment.

searches.name: Injection attempts that were NOT blocked
searches.description: Prompts from this actor that AI Defense allowed through - the guardrail gap.
searches.spl:
index=gen_ai_log `exclude_scoring_sourcetypes` (gen_ai.user.id="<actor>" OR enduser.id="<actor>") gen_ai.policy.blocked="false"
| table _time, gen_ai.session.id, gen_ai.app.name, gen_ai.request.model, prompt_category, gen_ai.safety.violated, gen_ai.pii.detected
| sort - _time

tasks.name: Assess data exposure
tasks.description:
Determine whether any response in the affected sessions returned sensitive data. Check PII/PHI detection and safety violation flags across the actor's full session set.

If PII or PHI was returned, trigger the organisation's data breach notification process in parallel with this plan.

searches.name: Data exposure by session
searches.description: PII/PHI detections and safety violations across the actor's sessions.
searches.spl:
index=gen_ai_log `exclude_scoring_sourcetypes` (gen_ai.user.id="<actor>" OR enduser.id="<actor>")
| stats sum(eval(if('gen_ai.pii.detected'="true",1,0))) AS pii_events, sum(eval(if('gen_ai.safety.violated'="true",1,0))) AS safety_violations, values(gen_ai.pii.types) AS pii_types BY gen_ai.session.id
| where pii_events > 0 OR safety_violations > 0

tasks.name: Inactivate the offending identity's account
tasks.description:
Stop further attempts from this actor.

**Containment standard:** 3 or more blocked prompt-injection attempts within 24 hours from one actor, with no authorized-testing record for that actor, means the account is inactivated pending review. The finding's `injection_attempts` and `policy_blocks` counts are the evidence; the note on this task is the review record.

Run the attached SOAR action **MedAdvice Identity Provider -> disable user** with the username from the finding's `user` field (the actor). The result is recorded on this task and on the investigation's Automation tab, and `enable user` on the same app reverses it during Recovery.

NOTE: the MedAdvice Identity Provider is a workshop simulator - every result carries "simulated": true and no directory is touched. On a stack without a paired SOAR, run the adaptive response action Suspend User (AI Defense) instead; it is equally simulated and records its audit entry in gen_ai_log under sourcetype ai_cim:response:action.

soar_binding.name: Inactivate account (MedAdvice IdP, simulated)
soar_binding.description: Disable the actor's account in the simulated MedAdvice identity provider. Username comes from the finding's user field; every result carries simulated=true.

parameters.reason: GenAI prompt injection containment - AI Incident Response Plan

tasks.name: Revoke active sessions and API credentials
tasks.description:
Invalidate anything the actor could reuse, including tokens issued before the account was inactivated.

Run the attached SOAR action **MedAdvice Identity Provider -> clear user sessions** for the same username. Repeat per session if the Identification phase found more than one application session.

Without a paired SOAR, run the adaptive response action Revoke Session / API Key instead. The same "simulated": true caveat applies as for account inactivation.

soar_binding.name: Revoke DemoBot sessions (MedAdvice IdP, simulated)
soar_binding.description: Revoke the actor's active application sessions in the simulated MedAdvice identity provider. Every result carries simulated=true.

parameters.reason: GenAI prompt injection containment - AI Incident Response Plan

tasks.name: Tighten the guardrail profile
tasks.description:
Close the gap for the specific technique observed, so the same prompt family is blocked for every user, not just this one.

Run the adaptive response action: Tighten Guardrail Policy

Scope it to the application identified in the finding. If the Identification phase found prompts that were allowed through, this task is mandatory before the incident can move to Recovery.

tasks.name: Confirm containment took effect
tasks.description:
Verify the actions were recorded and that no new activity is arriving from the actor.

Run both attached searches. A non-zero count from "Confirm activity has stopped" means containment has not held - return to the account inactivation task.

searches.name: Containment audit trail
searches.description: Response actions recorded against this actor, including their simulated/real status.
searches.spl:
index=gen_ai_log sourcetype=ai_cim:response:action target="<actor>"
| table _time, action_label, target_type, target, status, simulated, executed_by, execution_id

searches.name: Confirm activity has stopped
searches.description: Event count for the actor in the last 15 minutes. Non-zero means containment has not held.
searches.spl:
index=gen_ai_log `exclude_scoring_sourcetypes` (gen_ai.user.id="<actor>" OR enduser.id="<actor>") earliest=-15m
| stats count

tasks.name: Update the AI Defense policy
tasks.description:
Work with the AI platform owner to make the guardrail change permanent rather than incident-scoped. Capture the policy name and the classification that should now fire, so the change is reviewable.

Record the policy version before and after in the task notes.

tasks.name: Tune prompt filters and detection thresholds
tasks.description:
Feed the observed technique back into detection. If the injection used a pattern the correlation rule did not match, update the regex in AI Governance - Prompt Injection Attack Correlation - Rule.

If the campaign produced excessive findings for a single actor, review alert.suppress settings on that detection rather than weakening the pattern.

tasks.name: Verify no residual access
tasks.description: Run the attached search over a window that starts after containment. Confirm zero blocked and zero allowed events for the actor, across every application identified in the Identification phase.

searches.name: Residual access check
searches.description: Blocked and allowed event counts per application for the actor after containment.
searches.spl:
index=gen_ai_log `exclude_scoring_sourcetypes` (gen_ai.user.id="<actor>" OR enduser.id="<actor>")
| stats count BY gen_ai.app.name, gen_ai.policy.blocked

tasks.name: Restore normal access
tasks.description:
If the actor is a legitimate user whose account was misused rather than the attacker themselves, coordinate credential reset and restore access. Document the justification in the task notes.

If the actor is confirmed malicious, leave the suspension in place and record the decision instead.

tasks.name: Map the incident to AI threat frameworks
tasks.description:
Classify against OWASP LLM Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS so the incident aggregates with comparable events.

Baseline mapping for prompt injection:
- OWASP LLM Top 10: LLM01 (Prompt Injection)
- MITRE ATLAS: AML.T0051 (LLM Prompt Injection)

Adjust if the campaign also achieved data exposure or model exfiltration, and record the final mapping.

tasks.name: Feed lessons learned into detection
tasks.description:
Close the loop on detection fidelity. Note which signal fired first, whether the risk threshold was crossed on the intended actor, and whether any attempt evaded the correlation rule entirely.

If a technique was missed, capture the exact prompt pattern so it can be added to the detection and to the prompt injection training corpus.

tasks.name: Complete the incident record
tasks.description: Confirm the audit trail is complete before closing: every containment action recorded, every task noted, disposition set, and the response actions' simulated/real status stated explicitly.

searches.name: Full response action audit for the incident
searches.description: Complete action audit trail for the incident record.
searches.spl:
index=gen_ai_log sourcetype=ai_cim:response:action target="<actor>"
| table _time, action, action_label, target_type, target, status, simulated, executed_by, search_name, execution_id
| sort _time
